title: Picnic bands and the Owls at the Halfway House
summary: He recalls pickup bands and joining the Owls Orchestra with Eddie Miller and Bill Padron.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Who did you play with out there? Do you remember?

Um, well, uh, pick up bands, Dick. Nothing in particular. You know in those days, somebody called you up for a job. You never cared. You didn't much care, no matter who it was. It was just the idea that you had a, you were going to play out at a picnic. And you didn't pay much attention to really who it was. Uh, I remember playing out there with a fellow by name, uh, Early. Played bass. Have you ever taught him that name? Tom Early, yes.

He played, he played bass on some of the picnics that I played out there with. Uh, Angie Jumeli played on some of them out there. He played Sousa Porn out there. Uh, some of the trumpet players, I think, were Tony Foucherai. And, uh, Red Bowman, trumpet player. Incidentally, speaking of trumpet players, you must forget, uh, Bill Padron. Bill Padron played fine trumpet. I played with him with the Owls Orchestra, you know. I joined the Owls when they were at the halfway house. That's when Eddie Miller was playing with them. Angelo Palmezano was playing banjo. Frank Neto was playing bass. And Dan LeBlanc was playing tenor sax. Eddie Miller was playing outdoor sax. Dan LeBlanc was playing tenor sax. I didn't know that. Dan LeBlanc was a fine musician. He's a very underrated man. And he also plays wonderful bass too. Sure does. You can hear that. I don't know that. I don't know that. I don't know that.
I don't know that. I don't know that.
I don't know that. I don't know that. I don't know that. You didn't record with them. No, I didn't record with them at the Owls. The Owls.
No, my first records were with Shawkey Banana in 1936 when Shawkey Banana came with me.
He was a very underrated man. And he also plays wonderful bass too. Sure does.
You can hear that on the record. He played great tuba.

Yeah. Very good man. That must have been pretty late then after that. I joined the Owls at the halfway house in 1928 I think it was. And played with them quite awhile. You didn't record with them. No, I didn't record with them at the Owls.
No, I didn't record with them at the Owls.
